payload.claim: `apply_exported_patch` treats every non-zero exit from `git apply --index -` as `CriticPatchApplyFailed`, which `_drive_cell` unconditionally converts to `EXHAUSTED` (task's own fault, charged to it). But `worktree.DIFF_FLAGS` carries no `--binary` (documented at `.saffron/specs/done/SA-0069-...md:196` and `tests/test_package.py:450`), so `export_patch` renders any binary-file change as a non-appliable `Binary files ... differ` stub. `package.py`'s own `apply_patch` hits this identical limitation and is treated as infrastructure (`PackageError`, exit 2, charged to nobody) — the precedent this diff's docstring at line 978-981 contradicts by declaring every apply failure 'the task's failure, never `GATE_ERROR`'. A task that legitimately touches a binary file (an image fixture, a lockfile, a compiled asset) will now be marked `EXHAUSTED` and billed to the agent for a tooling gap that predates this change and that `saffron/cell/worktree.py` is explicitly out of scope to fix here. The tests only stub `exec_stream`'s return code and never exercise a real binary diff, so this holds in fixtures but not in a real target repo.
